reviews.title: Misleading $400 Coupon Offer – A Complete Scam and Disappointment
reviews.text:
I honestly feel this is a complete scam and a very misleading offer. SHEIN advertised that I could receive $400 worth of coupons by purchasing an item for just $0.50. Based on that offer, I purchased an item costing around $1, even though I didn’t really need it.

However, after making the purchase, I was informed that I would only qualify for the $400 coupons if I spent another $40 or more on additional items. To make matters worse, the $400 is not given as one coupon but is divided into six separate coupons, each with its own minimum spending requirement.

This is extremely misleading and feels like a trap to encourage customers to keep spending more money. If these conditions had been clearly explained from the beginning, I would never have made the purchase.

I have been a SHEIN customer and have shopped with them before, but this experience has completely changed my opinion. I feel cheated and disappointed. I will never shop with SHEIN again. Customers deserve honest and transparent offers, not promotions that make them spend more money under false expectations.

reviews.title: The price
reviews.text:
The prices advertised on SHEIN are misleading. Items show one price when browsing, but as soon as you add them to your cart, the prices increase significantly. For example, an item advertised for $7–$8 suddenly becomes $13–$16 each.

I’ve used my calculator multiple times to compare my total with the amount SHEIN charges, and the difference is consistently $30–$40 more than expected.

This is not a small discrepancy. Customers should not have to discover completely different prices at checkout. This is not a small discrepancy. Customers should not have to discover completely different prices at checkout. Advertising low prices to attract customers and then significantly increasing them in the cart feels deceptive and like clickbait pricing.

SHEIN needs to be transparent about its actual prices. Customers deserve to know what they’re paying before adding items to their carts.

I normally wear an XL in shorts, but the XL shorts I got from shein fit on me like a medium or a large, you can literally see my unmentionables. The app also incentivises you to spend more with dodgy deals, for example I had an offer for five free items if I placed an order immediately, however I was never given the chance to check out with those items. Also they have this game you can play where you take care of a dog, where the more you feed it the more a bar fills up, and when the bar is full you’re supposed to get a free gift or store credit, however it’s designed so it’s impossible to win.

Also my package came with a small handwritten note that said “We are dying” so I think I’ll pass on future shein orders.

reviews.title: Prices are not Accurate it’s keep changing it
reviews.text:
I’ve found the SHEIN shopping experience quite frustrating lately. The prices don’t always seem accurate or consistent, as they keep changing, which makes it difficult to know what you’re actually paying for. There also seems to be a lot of confusion around the products, with so many similar items being displayed at once. It can make it quite difficult to find exactly what you’re looking for, especially when there are so many advertisements and promotional offers appearing throughout the app.

Another thing I find frustrating is the constant encouragement to sign up for the membership. The membership offers and coupons don’t always seem as worthwhile as they are made to appear, and the terms can be difficult to understand. The membership benefits and coupons should be much more straightforward, with clear information about what you’re actually getting and any restrictions that apply.

Overall, SHEIN has a huge range of products and affordable options, but the shopping experience could be much better if the pricing was more consistent, the product selection was less overwhelming, and the membership and coupon system was simpler and more transparent

reviews.title: Misleading discounts, confusing app and poor transparency‼️🚨
reviews.text:
SHEIN’s app feels designed to confuse and pressure customers into spending more. It is overloaded with pop_ups, countdowns, “exclusive” rewards, adverts and fake urgency, making shopping exhausting instead of simple.

The discounts feel misleading. Prices are crossed out to make it look like you are saving a huge amount, but it is often unclear whether those original prices are real or whether anyone actually pays them. The £200 credit offer is especially misleading: it looks like a simple reward, but the small print shows you have to place multiple extra orders, check in daily and keep spending money before unlocking it. That is not a straightforward £200 reward, it is a tactic to push customers into buying more.

The app is also unclear about the real final price. There are too many coupons, promotions, wallet credits and banners competing at once, so it is difficult to understand what is genuinely a discount and what is just marketing.

Product photos can also be misleading. I had to keep checking customer comments and real customer photos to see what items actually look like before buying, because the official photos often look much better, clearer or different from reality.

Shopping should feel transparent and trustworthy. Instead, SHEIN feels cluttered, manipulative and more expensive than it first appears! 🚨‼️
